newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar edges higher amid supply concern.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar edges higher amid supply concern.

text.p: White sugar futures nudged gently higher on Friday as trade players continued to buy into the spot August contract amid concern over dwindling summer availability, traders said.
Although one leading trade house was mentioned as an August buyer, commission houses also featuring on the buy side were thought to be acting for other trade clients, they said.

Concern over seasonal physical tightness has prompted a persistent stream of buying in recent weeks as the market fears reduced supply between the tail-end of the European crop and the start of the 1997/98 beet campaign.

"The whites are steady...and it's going to carry on being steady. All the trade are buying it," said one, adding that both the outright spot position and the August/October spread were attracting buying interest.
"You've got to be long of the spread and be long of the whites in general because it's going to be steady for the next couple of months," he said.
August/October, while not particularly active on Friday morning, has gradually widened to between $10.50 and $11.00 from around $8.50 a couple of weeks ago.
At 1130 GMT August was up 60 cents at $324.50, just 50 cents off its intraday high, and October was up 40 cents at $314.00. Volume was concentrated in August and totalled 523 lots.
All traded Paris positions were also higher in a light overall volume of 105 lots.
August was up $1.30 at $324.70 and October was up $2.30 at $314.80.
